feature: Falls / function — complementary CDC STEADI assessments

current_resource.authority: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention / National Center for Injury Prevention and Control
current_resource.program: STEADI — Stopping Elderly Accidents, Deaths & Injuries

brazil_boundary.software_rule: Present every STEADI assessment as complementary international guidance below or separately from the Brazilian national layer.

durable_boundaries.finding: CDC STEADI is complementary international guidance for this application; the current Brazilian national layer remains Caderneta 2026 plus IVCF-20.
durable_boundaries.software_rule: Never present STEADI as the national SUS default or replace the Brazil-primary instruments.

durable_boundaries.finding: TUG, Chair Stand, 4-Stage Balance, orthostatic BP, Caderneta and IVCF-20 are distinct assessments.
durable_boundaries.software_rule: Never add their outputs into a synthetic fall-risk score and never infer one instrument's result from another.

durable_boundaries.finding: STEADI TUG is a 3-m/10-ft stand-walk-turn-return-sit test; IVCF-20 contains a separate 4-m gait condition.
durable_boundaries.software_rule: Never relabel the IVCF-20 4-m gait item as TUG or reuse its >5-second finding as the STEADI >=12-second TUG threshold.

durable_boundaries.finding: The CDC 30-Second Chair Stand reference table supplied by STEADI spans ages 60 through 94.
durable_boundaries.software_rule: Do not extrapolate age/sex cutoffs beyond age 94. Outside the source table, return the raw stand count without a STEADI below-average classification.

durable_boundaries.finding: Chair Stand values are below average only when the repetition count is strictly less than the age/sex threshold.
durable_boundaries.software_rule: A count exactly equal to the published threshold must not be classified as below average.

durable_boundaries.finding: The 4-Stage Balance handout instructs that an assistive device is not used during the test.
durable_boundaries.software_rule: Do not silently apply TUG's walking-aid allowance to the 4-Stage Balance Test.

durable_boundaries.finding: The STEADI orthostatic protocol specifies 5 minutes supine and standing measurements at 1 and 3 minutes; the 2026 Brazilian Caderneta does not itself define that full timing/cutoff protocol.
durable_boundaries.software_rule: Label the timing and 20/10-mmHg-or-symptom interpretation as STEADI complementary guidance, not as a Caderneta/SUS numeric rule.

implementation_order: Python engines with each instrument separate
bilingual UI below/separate from Brazil-primary layer
